performance.scope: Six fresh processes per runtime and all source-load permutations. Twelve balanced common >=20ms batches per workflow, same-source duplicate, pre-timing numerical/alias/caller-state checks. Seventeen existing public0.70API flows (including publicVJP/Jacobian) and three analytically validated HVP compositions of released0.70 public AD primitives. No nativeTorch/GPU/cold-start/universal speedup claim.

findings: All18freshchildren and20flows passed exact-source,program,numerical,dtype,shape,alias and caller-state gates.

Existing17API B/A medians0.9858–1.0224 with same-source A/A0.9855–1.0245; worst candidate/duplicate median1.0120. No material persistent legacy regression requiring additional controls was identified within this experiment. This is not a universal no-regression claim.

New functionalHVP flows cost about2.1%–5.7% more than validated0.70 publicAD compositions; this is feature overhead versus a composed reference,not a released0.70functionalHVP API or isolated-cause measurement.

Three CPU float64 sin objectives use direct/dense tracked peaks0.1328,0.06046,0.02818 with dense A/A1.0. Dense reference is built from the same selected HVP basis calls; not RSS,WASM/GPU memory,latency or universal gain.
The prior piecewise-release measurements remain historical and do not substitute for this corrected-source run.

cpu_allocations.scope: One CPU process, three real float64 sin objectives, six balanced call orders and repeated dense A/A control. Dense reference assembles a full Hessian from the selected library HVP basis calls; it is not a released0.70 API or a different derivative implementation. Tracks Python/NumPy allocations only, not RSS or WASM/GPU memory. Not a latency benchmark.

limitations: Detached real float32/64 HVP results only; create_graph,complex,nested forward AD and unsupported forward rules reject. No GPU backend.

676 direct native cases include expected errors;4 FP32 normalization cases use independent analytic/native-FP64 controls;40 determinant cases deliberately provide finite polynomial curvature where the native SVD tape gives NaNs.

HVP latency reference is a validated composition of released0.70 public AD primitives, not a public0.70 functional HVP API. Interpret exact measured ratios together with both A/A denominators and the recorded review.
Allocation evidence is one CPU process,three float64 sin objectives;dense reference assembles a Hessian from the same selected HVP basis calls. Not RSS,WASM/GPU memory,latency or a universal gain.
Archive preserves rejected earlier candidates and failures with their original source/version identities. Scripts retain absolute paths and require dependency setup/path adjustment.
Local validation does not imply main adoption,CI,release or deployment.
